algorithm.Title: Ear - Swimmer's - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: Qatar-localized UAT-only adult and pediatric pathway for suspected otitis externa after water exposure, screening for invasive infection, diabetes/immunocompromise, hearing or neurologic complications; not approved for production.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 and do not drive. Keep the patient observed and the ear dry; insert nothing and use no drops while awaiting emergency assessment. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
algorithm.Author: IST Health Open-Source Guideline Content
algorithm.LastRevised: RESEARCH_REQUIRED - internal IST clinical adaptation date is not recorded

questions.Question: Is there ear pain without recent swimming, water exposure, or outer-ear canal inflammation?
questions.Information: Ear pain not associated with water exposure or an inflamed ear canal belongs in the general Earache pathway.

questions.Question: Is there confusion, reduced responsiveness, rapid deterioration, facial weakness, severe pain with diabetes or immune suppression, or redness/swelling spreading around or behind the ear with marked systemic illness?
questions.Information: These features may indicate sepsis, invasive external-ear infection or cranial-nerve involvement and require emergency assessment.

questions.Question: Does the person feel generally unwell or have a very high temperature, is there swelling around the ear, fluid coming from the ear, hearing loss or change, nausea/vomiting/dizziness, a severe sore throat, or a weakened immune system?
questions.Information: NHS.UK ear infection guidance lists these as urgent clinical-review criteria.

questions.Question: Has earache persisted beyond 3 days, or are ear infections recurring?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends a primary-care review for persistent or recurrent ear infections.

questions.Question: After higher-risk features are excluded, is swimmer's ear still suspected without direct canal and eardrum examination?
questions.Information: The cited source is not specific to otitis externa and safe drops depend on eardrum status; this UAT pathway requires in-person examination.

advice.Title: Emergency invasive ear-infection precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 and do not drive. Keep the patient observed and the ear dry; insert nothing and use no drops while awaiting emergency assessment. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: confusion or reduced responsiveness; facial weakness or rapidly spreading swelling.

advice.Title: Urgent ear infection review
Content: Arrange same-day medical review for these symptoms.
Call Back If: worsening pain or swelling; fever develops.

advice.Title: Routine ear infection follow-up
Content: Arrange a primary-care review for persistent or recurring ear infections.
Call Back If: symptoms worsen; new discharge.

advice.Title: In-person assessment for suspected swimmer's ear
Content: Keep the ear dry, avoid swimming and do not insert objects or use drops until the canal and eardrum are examined. Arrange prompt in-person assessment through the Qatar UAT pathway.
Call Back If: pain or swelling worsens; fever, hearing change, discharge, dizziness or facial weakness.
